DISSEMINATED_TB.title: Miliary (spread-out) tuberculosis

items: Miliary tuberculosis is TB that spreads through the blood to many organs.
It is serious and needs early diagnosis.
Fever, night sweats, poor appetite, weakness, and weight loss.
An enlarged liver or spleen in some people.
Chest X-ray or CT. A normal X-ray does not rule it out.
Blood cultures for mycobacteria and sputum or fluid samples.
A liver or bone marrow biopsy if other tests do not give an answer.
An eye examination for small spots (choroidal tubercles) in some people.
An HIV test.
Your doctor will start TB treatment once the diagnosis is likely.
Your team will explain the plan and tests needed.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Take medicines as prescribed, and ask before changing anything.
Tell your team about any close contact with TB.
Regular blood tests and scans are often needed during treatment.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Confusion, drowsiness, fits, or new weakness
Fever with feeling faint or very unwell

ENTERIC_FEVER.title: Enteric fever (typhoid)

items: Enteric fever, also called typhoid, is a bacterial infection spread through contaminated food or water.
It causes a long fever that rises step by step.
A fever that climbs over several days and stays high for about 10 to 14 days.
Headache, poor appetite, belly discomfort, and sometimes constipation or diarrhoea.
Pink spots (rose spots) on the chest or belly in some people.
Blood culture, the main test. Several cultures may be needed.
Blood count and liver tests.
Stool or urine culture.
Your doctor will choose antibiotics based on the culture and local patterns.
Some people need a longer course or hospital care.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Drink safe, boiled or bottled water, and wash hands often.
Eat well-cooked food.
Your team may repeat blood and stool tests to confirm you are clear of the infection.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Confusion, severe belly pain, or a swollen tender belly
Fainting, or very low blood pressure
